findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "what_changed" stacks urgency/override words (urgent, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_publications, get_publication, check_originality_and_fit, get_order_status, start_radar, get_gaps, mark_fix_done, check_request · Private data: answer_question, start_fix, mark_fix_done, check_request, rate_fix, get_reputation_profile, update_reputation_profile · Public sink: find_publications, check_originality_and_fit, set_preferences, check_request · Destructive: start_radar.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_publications, get_publication, check_originality_and_fit, get_order_status, start_radar, get_gaps, mark_fix_done, check_request · Private data: answer_question, start_fix, mark_fix_done, check_request, rate_fix, get_reputation_profile, update_reputation_profile · Public sink: find_publications, check_originality_and_fit, set_preferences, check_request · Destructive: start_radar

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
